info.title: Cartesia Managed Agents WebSocket API
info.description: Stream audio and events between an application and a Managed Agent. Server applications authenticate with `X-API-Key`; browser and mobile applications pass an `access_token` query parameter. See the [WebSocket guide](/line/integrations/websocket-api) for setup, limits, and audio handling.

agent_id.description: ID of the managed agent to connect to.

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: API key for trusted server applications.

accessToken.name: access_token
accessToken.description: Short-lived token for browser and mobile applications.

AgentSessionCreateEvent.name: AgentSessionCreateEvent
AgentSessionCreateEvent.title: Session Create
AgentSessionCreateEvent.description: Configures the session's audio. **This must be the first message sent.** The server closes the connection if any other event arrives first, or if no event arrives within 10 seconds. Unknown fields are rejected.

AgentAudioInputEvent.name: AgentAudioInputEvent
AgentAudioInputEvent.title: Audio Input
AgentAudioInputEvent.description: Streams user audio to the agent. Send chunks continuously (for example every 20–100 ms) for the best latency. `audio` must be base64-encoded audio in the format declared in `session_create.audio.input_format`. Wait for `session_ready` before sending audio; audio sent earlier is dropped.

AgentDtmfInputEvent.name: AgentDtmfInputEvent
AgentDtmfInputEvent.title: DTMF Input
AgentDtmfInputEvent.description: Sends a DTMF (dual-tone multi-frequency) digit to the agent.

AgentClientToolResultEvent.name: AgentClientToolResultEvent
AgentClientToolResultEvent.title: Client Tool Result
AgentClientToolResultEvent.description: Answers a `client_tool_call` whose `expects_response` is `true`. `tool_call_id` must match the call being answered. The decoded `result` may be at most 4096 bytes; larger results are replaced with a `result_too_large` error result. Late, duplicate, or mismatched results are ignored.

AgentSessionReadyEvent.name: AgentSessionReadyEvent
AgentSessionReadyEvent.title: Session Ready
AgentSessionReadyEvent.description: Sent once after `session_create`, when the agent pipeline can accept audio. Reports the call record created for this session and the agent version the session is pinned to. Use `call_id` with the [calls API](/api-reference/agents/calls/get-call) to fetch the recording and transcript after the call.

AgentAudioOutputEvent.name: AgentAudioOutputEvent
AgentAudioOutputEvent.title: Audio Output
AgentAudioOutputEvent.description: The agent's speech. `audio` is base64-encoded audio in the format declared in `session_create.audio.input_format`.

AgentAudioOutputClearEvent.name: AgentAudioOutputClearEvent
AgentAudioOutputClearEvent.title: Audio Output Clear
AgentAudioOutputClearEvent.description: Sent when the user starts speaking. Discard buffered agent audio and stop playback. The event can arrive while no agent audio is playing, in which case there is nothing to clear.

AgentDtmfOutputEvent.name: AgentDtmfOutputEvent
AgentDtmfOutputEvent.title: DTMF Output
AgentDtmfOutputEvent.description: A DTMF digit the agent sends, for clients bridging a telephony system.

AgentClientToolCallEvent.name: AgentClientToolCallEvent
AgentClientToolCallEvent.title: Client Tool Call
AgentClientToolCallEvent.description: The agent asks this client to run a client tool. When `expects_response` is `true`, answer with a `client_tool_result` carrying the same `tool_call_id`; the invocation stays open until a result, error, or timeout. When `false`, dispatching the action completes the invocation.

AgentTurnStartedEvent.name: AgentTurnStartedEvent
AgentTurnStartedEvent.title: Turn Started
AgentTurnStartedEvent.description: Sent when the user starts speaking or the agent starts responding. `turn` comes from a single counter shared by both roles, starting at 1 and strictly increasing over the call, so `turn` alone identifies a turn.

AgentTurnOutputTextDeltaEvent.name: AgentTurnOutputTextDeltaEvent
AgentTurnOutputTextDeltaEvent.title: Turn Text Delta
AgentTurnOutputTextDeltaEvent.description: Sent as the agent speaks, carrying the text spoken since the previous delta, typically one word at a time. Deltas include separator spaces, so build the running text by appending `text` verbatim. The user's speech is not streamed incrementally. It arrives as finalized text in `turn_ended`.

AgentTurnEndedEvent.name: AgentTurnEndedEvent
AgentTurnEndedEvent.title: Turn Ended
AgentTurnEndedEvent.description: Sent when a turn finishes, with the complete final text for the turn. This is the version to store and display. The events for a single turn always arrive in order: `turn_started`, then any `turn_output_text_delta` events, then `turn_ended`. If the agent hangs up mid-turn, the connection closes without a final `turn_ended`; treat the close as ending any open turn.

AgentErrorEvent.name: AgentErrorEvent
AgentErrorEvent.title: Error
AgentErrorEvent.description: Reports a problem with the session or an event you sent. When `fatal` is `false`, the server ignores that event and keeps the connection open. When `fatal` is `true`, it closes the connection with code 1008 for client or protocol errors, or 1011 if the agent fails.

input_format.description: Format of the audio your client sends. Agent audio is returned in the same format. Required, because a sample rate that mismatches your capture format fails silently as garbled audio.

output_delivery.description: How the server delivers agent audio. `speaking_pace` paces audio to playback speed. `as_available` sends it as fast as the model produces it, so a client that buffers locally can play it back on its own clock for lower latency. Not supported when the agent uses a background sound.

dynamic_variables.description:
Custom [dynamic variable](/agents/dynamic-variables) values for this session.

Names are case-sensitive, up to 64 characters, and use letters, digits, or underscores. `system__` and `secret__` prefixes are reserved.

AgentSessionCreateEvent.description: Configures the session's audio. **This must be the first message sent.** The server closes the connection if any other event arrives first, or if no event arrives within 10 seconds. Unknown fields are rejected.

audio.description: Base64-encoded audio in the format declared in `session_create.audio.input_format`.

AgentAudioInputEvent.description: Streams user audio to the agent. Send chunks continuously (for example every 20–100 ms) for the best latency. `audio` must be base64-encoded audio in the format declared in `session_create.audio.input_format`. Wait for `session_ready` before sending audio; audio sent earlier is dropped.

digit.description: A single DTMF digit, one of `0`-`9`, `*`, or `#`.

AgentDtmfInputEvent.description: Sends a DTMF (dual-tone multi-frequency) digit to the agent.

result.description: The tool's result, as a string the model can read. At most 4096 bytes decoded.

is_error.description: Set to `true` when the tool failed. The LLM receives `result` as a normal string; Cartesia logs the failure and uses a generic message if `result` is empty.

error_type.description: Optional free-form string, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes. Cartesia logs this; the LLM does not see it.

AgentClientToolResultEvent.description: Answers a `client_tool_call` whose `expects_response` is `true`. `tool_call_id` must match the call being answered. The decoded `result` may be at most 4096 bytes; larger results are replaced with a `result_too_large` error result. Late, duplicate, or mismatched results are ignored.

call_id.description: Identifier of the call record created for this session. Use it with the calls API to fetch the recording and transcript after the call.

agent_version_id.description: The agent version this session is pinned to, which is the version published when the connection opened.

input_format.description: The accepted input format, echoed from `session_create`.

AgentSessionReadyEvent.description: Sent once after `session_create`, when the agent pipeline can accept audio. Reports the call record created for this session and the agent version the session is pinned to. Use `call_id` with the [calls API](/api-reference/agents/calls/get-call) to fetch the recording and transcript after the call.

audio.description: Base64-encoded agent audio in the format declared in `session_create.audio.input_format`.

AgentAudioOutputEvent.description: The agent's speech. `audio` is base64-encoded audio in the format declared in `session_create.audio.input_format`.

AgentAudioOutputClearEvent.description: Sent when the user starts speaking. Discard buffered agent audio and stop playback. The event can arrive while no agent audio is playing, in which case there is nothing to clear.

digit.description: A single DTMF digit, one of `0`-`9`, `*`, or `#`.

AgentDtmfOutputEvent.description: A DTMF digit the agent sends, for clients bridging a telephony system.

tool_call_id.description: Identifies this invocation. Echo it in `client_tool_result`.

tool_name.description: Name of the client tool to run.

parameters.description: Arguments for the tool, matching the tool's parameter schema.

expects_response.description: Whether the agent waits for a `client_tool_result`. Comes from the tool's definition.

AgentClientToolCallEvent.description: The agent asks this client to run a client tool. When `expects_response` is `true`, answer with a `client_tool_result` carrying the same `tool_call_id`; the invocation stays open until a result, error, or timeout. When `false`, dispatching the action completes the invocation.

turn.description: Turn index, unique across the call.

start_time.description: Seconds since the start of the session.

AgentTurnStartedEvent.description: Sent when the user starts speaking or the agent starts responding. `turn` comes from a single counter shared by both roles, starting at 1 and strictly increasing over the call, so `turn` alone identifies a turn.

turn.description: Matches the `turn` of the turn the text belongs to.

text.description: The exact substring to append. Separator spaces are included, so build the running text with `buffer[turn] += text`.

AgentTurnOutputTextDeltaEvent.description: Sent as the agent speaks, carrying the text spoken since the previous delta, typically one word at a time. Deltas include separator spaces, so build the running text by appending `text` verbatim. The user's speech is not streamed incrementally. It arrives as finalized text in `turn_ended`.

turn.description: Matches the `turn` of the corresponding `turn_started` event.

text.description: The finalized text of the turn. For a user turn, the transcribed speech. For an assistant turn, the text the agent actually spoke.

interrupted.description: For assistant turns, `true` when the user interrupted the turn. For user turns, `true` only when the call ended mid-turn.

start_time.description: Seconds since the start of the session.

end_time.description: Seconds since the start of the session.

result.description: The tool's result, when one was recorded.

dynamic_variable_updates.description: Values assigned by this tool. Omitted when the tool assigned no values.

old_value.description: Previous value, or null if the variable had no value

updated_at.description: Time of the update, in seconds since the call started

tool_id.description: ID of the configured tool that assigned the value

tool_call_id.description: ID of the tool call that assigned the value, matching `tool_calls[].id`

AgentTurnEndedEvent.description: Sent when a turn finishes, with the complete final text for the turn. This is the version to store and display. The events for a single turn always arrive in order: `turn_started`, then any `turn_output_text_delta` events, then `turn_ended`. If the agent hangs up mid-turn, the connection closes without a final `turn_ended`; treat the close as ending any open turn.

code.description:
`invalid_event` means a client event was rejected; `agent_failed` means the agent failed. The following errors prevent the session from starting:

- `missing_dynamic_variables`: a value needed by the welcome message is missing.
- `invalid_dynamic_variables`: the supplied names or values are invalid.
- `dynamic_variables_not_allowed`: a browser access token was used to supply custom values.

fatal.description: Whether the server closes the connection after this error.

AgentErrorEvent.description: Reports a problem with the session or an event you sent. When `fatal` is `false`, the server ignores that event and keeps the connection open. When `fatal` is `true`, it closes the connection with code 1008 for client or protocol errors, or 1011 if the agent fails.
